newsitem.title: JORDAN: National Bank bloc sale buttresses Amman bourse.
newsitem.headline: National Bank bloc sale buttresses Amman bourse.

text.p: A large bloc sale on National Bank on Sunday helped buttress the Amman bourse amid signs of an upward trend on popular blue-chips sparked by so far limited foreign buying, dealers said.
"The market is generally stable with a slight improvement on certain stock," said senior analyst Mohammmed Abdullah, Pearl Consulting.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index rose 0.46 percent to 159.32 points in healthy turnover of 1.9 million dinars ($2.7 million).
More than half the value of daily trade was dominated by a bloc sale in Jordan National Bank, which rose 0.03 dinars to 2.12 dinars in a deal possibly executed by foreign buyers.

Brokers say the bourse is generally stable amid growing foreign interest which resurfaced since Saturday and could signal the start of a repeat pattern of select bargain buying on cement and mining firms which the bourse witnessed last month.
Prices have eased since gaining nearly six percent in the final week of May on the back of foreign fund buying.
"Foreign buying is picking up again on major blue-chip and demand is continuing," Abdullah added.
In pharamaceuticals, leading drug firm Dar al-Dawa also attracted some foreign inspired interest after prices gained 0.02 dinars to 5.51 dinars in the third busiest deal worth 106,802 dinars.

Jordan Kuwait Bank rose a high 0.17 dinars to 3.61 dinars in trade worth 60,118 dinars with no end in sight to a board room tussle between major shareholders after a failed takeover attempt by Bank of Jordan.
Jordan Cement, a popular foreign investor choice, rose 0.01 dinars to 4.03 dinars in trade worth 98,165 dinars.
Overall rising shares outnumbered losers on Sunday by 22 to seven, with another 23 trading but closing unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance rose 0.16 percent to 81.23 points, 2.59 percent down from the start of the year.
